headline: Profitability arrives as revenue growth holds steady
summary_short: Procore's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 15.8% y/y to $375.2 million, and the company swung to a $16.9 million net profit (diluted EPS $0.11) versus a $21.1 million loss a year ago, as non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 21% from 13%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 16% y/y to $375.2M (+4.4% q/q), 88% from existing customers, holding gross margin at 80%. Operating income turned positive at $4.3M; non-GAAP operating income was $80.5M (21% margin, up from 13%) as sales & marketing rose just 3% despite a 4% headcount cut, while G&A rose on $3.4M of incremental Oracle-litigation legal fees, partly offset by a $5.0M non-cash lease-modification gain. Net income was $16.9M ($0.11 diluted EPS) versus a $21.1M loss a year ago, aided by $3.9M of unrealized gains on strategic investments. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities rose to $655.9M. The company bought back $100.0M of stock YTD and, on July 27, agreed to acquire DroneDeploy for ~$845.0M. No forward guidance was disclosed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: revenue rose $51.3M y/y, ~88% from existing customers (renewals/expansions carrying a full quarter) and ~12% from new customers acquired in the quarter.
Company-disclosed: margin held near 80% as a $4.4M rise in capitalized-software amortization and a $2.6M rise in third-party hosting costs grew roughly in line with revenue.

Company-disclosed: return to positive operating income reflects 16% revenue growth against controlled opex — S&M up only 3% on a 4% headcount cut, G&A up 1% as Oracle-litigation legal fees were offset by a lease-modification gain.
Company-disclosed: swing to profit builds on the operating-income improvement plus a $3.9M rise in other income from unrealized gains on strategic investments and a $1.3M larger tax benefit.
Derived-arithmetic: diluted EPS improvement tracks the net-income swing; diluted share count rose only modestly (152.8M vs 149.7M), a small drag relative to the profit gain.

Company-disclosed: cRPO rose 22% y/y to $1.67B and customers over $100k ARR grew 14% y/y to 2,871, evidence cited for demand durability; on July 27 the company agreed to acquire DroneDeploy for ~$845M.
